blocks.h2: Signs Your Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Arlington Heights homeowners usually call us about one of these:

tiles.body: On a gas heater, it's often the pilot, thermocouple or gas valve. On an electric one, an element or thermostat.
Sediment on the bottom of the tank takes up space, or one heating element has quit.
A drip from a fitting or the relief valve is a repair. Water from the tank itself means replacement.

tiles.h3: Rumbling, Popping or a Rotten Egg Smell
tiles.body: Popping is sediment. A sulfur smell usually points to the anode rod reacting with the water.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: About 4 in 10 Arlington Heights homes were built in the 1970s and 1980s. Most are on their second or third water heater, and the setup around it is often as old as the house.

items.body: Many gas water heaters here still vent into an old masonry chimney. When the furnace gets upgraded and vents out the side wall, the water heater can be left venting alone into a chimney that's too big for it. We check the draft on every gas heater we touch.

items.h3: Basement Utility Rooms Next to Finished Space
items.body: Postwar and 1970s basements often have the heater in a corner next to a finished room. A slow leak can soak carpet and drywall before anyone notices. A drain pan and a leak sensor help.
The gas shutoff and water valves next to an old heater may not have been turned in decades. We check them before any repair, so you can shut the heater off when you need to.

bodies: We repair every type of water heater you'll find in an Arlington Heights home: standard gas and electric tanks, power-vent units, high-efficiency condensing heaters and tankless models. Every visit starts with a diagnosis, then a recommendation.

Before you call, find the label on the side of the tank. It lists the fuel, the size in gallons and the manufacture date, usually in the serial number. That tells us a lot about whether a repair makes sense. If it's time for a new one, see [water heater installation](/arlington-heights/water-heater-installation).

Even treated Lake Michigan water carries minerals that settle in the bottom of the tank. A yearly flush clears that sediment so the burner heats water instead of a layer of scale, and the heater runs quieter.

During a maintenance visit we flush the tank, test the temperature and pressure relief valve, check the anode rod and look at the burner or elements and the venting. Tankless units get descaled. If your heater has never been flushed, start with a maintenance visit.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

steps.body: We find the part that failed before we talk about price. If it's a repair, we say so.

steps.h3: 2. Repair vs. Replace, Side by Side
steps.body: When a heater is near the end, you see both options with prices and expected life.
One price before we start, and the utility room left as clean as we found it.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Why does my pilot light keep going out?
items.preview: Usually a worn thermocouple or a draft problem.
items.answer: Usually a worn thermocouple or flame sensor that no longer tells the gas valve the pilot is lit. A draft problem in the vent can also blow it out. Both are fixable, and we check the venting while we're there.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
items.preview: A leaking tank means replace. A failed part on a younger heater is usually a repair.
items.answer: If the tank itself is leaking, it needs replacing. If a part failed on a heater under about 8 years old, repair usually makes sense. If the repair is a big share of the cost of a new heater, we'll tell you.

items.q: How long do water heaters last in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: Tank heaters usually last about 8 to 12 years.
items.answer: Tank water heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years, depending on use and maintenance. Tankless units often last longer with regular descaling.

items.q: Is it dangerous if my water heater is leaking?
items.preview: Usually not dangerous, but it gets worse. Shut off the cold supply and call.
items.answer: A leak is rarely dangerous on its own, but it won't fix itself. Turn off the cold water valve above the tank, and for a gas heater set the control to pilot or off. If you smell gas, leave the house and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
